rationale.conceptual: The paper applies an established pair potential (Esterling–Swaroop) to compute anharmonic thermodynamic properties. The formulas are provided, but the agent must extract piecewise polynomial coefficients from two cited papers, determine equilibrium distances via energy minimization, evaluate high-order derivatives, and correctly apply low- and high-temperature heat capacity limits. This is a multi-part, documented algorithm that requires careful implementation, though no novel research-grade derivation is needed. Hence, it sits at level 3 (non-trivial but established).
rationale.execution: The pipeline has four stages: (1) fetch potential coefficients from two external references and compute derivatives, (2) compute Debye temperature and Grüneisen parameter using experimental bulk moduli, (3) compute auxiliary anharmonic parameters, (4) compute heat capacity and thermal expansion and assemble CSV. It involves sequential dependencies and external data acquisition (extracting numeric coefficients from papers), which adds fragility. Thus, it falls into the 3 range (multi-stage pipeline with dependencies and some data-fetch complexity).
